text.p: Martin Rodriguez, an Argentinian baseliner who had never won an ATP Tour match, scored the first upset of the week at the $289,250 U.S. Men's Clay Court Championships on Monday.
Rodriguez, a qualifier ranked 190, beat a below par MaliVai Washington, the tournament's second seed, 6-1 6-2 taking the luster off a field led by third-ranked Michael Chang, who plays on Tuesday.

Petr Korda of the Czech Republic, the third seed ranked 27th, recovered after losing the first set to unseeded American, Jeff Salzenstein, winning 2-6 6-4 4-3 when Salzenstein retired suffering leg cramps.
Fifth-seeded Jason Stoltenberg of Australia advanced to the second round, beating unseeded Armenian, Sargis Sargsian 6-1 7-5.

Washington, ranked 33, suffered a knee injury in Davis Cup play in early February and has played only sporadically since. On Monday his movement appeared severely hampered particularly on the serve, and he collapsed in a sea of unforced errors, losing the first set 6-1 in just 26 minutes.

The players exchanged service breaks five times at the start of the second set, but Rodriguez, a consistent groundstroker, looked more confident. The Argentinian tried risky dropshots from the baseline without success but used his smooth backhand to pass Washington at will, breaking twice to lead 3-2, then 5-2.
Rodriguez served out the match 6-2 as Washington offered no resistence, the American netting an easy forehand to give Rodriguez the victory.
"The tournament director could have pushed me today," said Washington, who said he knew his knee "wasn't going to be where I wanted it to be."

Washington said he had heard "about 50 opinions from different physicians, trainers and therapists," without any satisfactory diagnosis. "After you've heard 50 opinions you don't need to hear any more," he said.
"I didn't particularly enjoy tonight's match, especially when I knew I wouldn't be able to do everything possible to win," Washington said.
The inexperienced Rodriguez suffered an attack of nerves before successfully closing out the win.

"In the second set I see my chance and I was a little scared to finish the match," said Rodriguez, who had lost the only two previous times he had qualified for an ATP Tour event despite eight years as a professional. "But when I was able to break at 3-2 and held my serve it was okay."

A late bloomer who turned professional at 21, Rodriguez said his slow start was due to lack of funds. "Before I didn't have much money so I had to play in France for money," he said. "I only started playing professional full-time two years ago."
Despite Washington's injury, Rodriguez said the victory, "was very important for me."
